rules.text: Cache in layers with explicit ownership — CDN (static, hashed assets), HTTP (`ETag`/`Cache-Control`), application (keyed, TTL'd, tenant-scoped), DB — and measure hit rates.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Static assets have content-hashed filenames and Cache-Control
rules.text: Static assets have content-hashed filenames and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; **public** HTML is `no-cache` (revalidate — never `no-store`, which breaks bfcache, PERF-22); authenticated or sensitive responses are `no-store` (DATA-2). Compression (br/gzip) on text.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Images
rules.text: Images: modern formats (AVIF/WebP), `width`/`height` set (no layout shift), responsive `srcset`/`sizes`, `loading="lazy"` below the fold, `fetchpriority="high"` on the LCP image.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Fonts
rules.text: Fonts: self-hosted WOFF2, subset, `font-display: swap`, the 1–2 critical files preloaded; no more than two families.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: JavaScript budget enforced in CI
rules.text: JavaScript budget enforced in CI (`size-limit` / bundle analyzer); route-level code splitting; third-party scripts loaded `async`/`defer`, each one justified (it costs performance, privacy and CSP surface); no render-blocking scripts in `<head>`.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Real-user monitoring of Core Web Vitals
rules.text: Real-user monitoring of Core Web Vitals (`web-vitals` → analytics) so budgets are checked against real devices, not just Lighthouse.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Public pages are bfcache-eligible: no unload handlers and no…
rules.text: Public pages are **bfcache-eligible**: no `unload` handlers and no `Cache-Control: no-store` on public HTML (PERF-14). *Enforced by:* the Lighthouse bfcache audit.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Speculation Rules
rules.text: Speculation Rules (`eagerness: "moderate"`) prefetch/prerender public same-origin navigations — never authenticated or state-changing URLs.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: RUM reports INP with Long Animation Frame
rules.text: RUM reports INP with Long Animation Frame (LoAF) attribution so slow interactions point at a script.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: content-visibility
rules.text: `content-visibility: auto` on long off-screen sections and lists.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Next.js apps stream with loading.tsx/Suspense boundaries and run the…
rules.text: Next.js apps stream with `loading.tsx`/Suspense boundaries and run the bundle analyzer per PR against the PERF-17 budget.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Flutter
rules.text: Flutter: `const` constructors wherever possible; rebuild only what changed (`select`/granular providers, no `setState` at the root); heavy work (parsing, crypto, image processing) in an isolate (`compute`/`Isolate.run`); lists via `ListView.builder`; images decoded at display size (`cacheWidth`/`cacheHeight`); startup work deferred until after first frame.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Profile in profile/release mode on a real mid-tier device
rules.text: Profile in **profile/release mode** on a real mid-tier device (DevTools, Instruments, Android Studio profiler) — debug builds lie about performance.

rules.section: 3 · Optimized code
rules.title: Each stack's profiler is part of the toolkit and used before optimizing
rules.text: Each stack's profiler is part of the toolkit and used before optimizing: Go `pprof`, Node `--cpu-prof`/clinic, Python `py-spy`/`scalene`, Flutter DevTools, Chrome Performance panel, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for SQL. Regressions in PERF-1 budgets fail CI.

rules.section: 3B · Framework & platform compatibility
rules.title: One browser target per app, declared once in browserslist
rules.text: One browser target per app, declared once in `browserslist` (default `baseline widely available`) and shared by the build, lint (`eslint-plugin-compat`) and CSS tooling. Vite's `build.target` doesn't read browserslist — set it explicitly to match. When a framework's own floor is stricter (Tailwind v4: Safari 16.4+), the stricter floor wins and is the declared target.

rules.section: 3B · Framework & platform compatibility
rules.title: Node is pinned to an Active or Maintenance LTS line in .nvmrc,…
rules.text: Node is pinned to an Active or Maintenance **LTS** line in `.nvmrc`, `engines`, `packageManager` and CI, with `engine-strict=true`; an odd-numbered or EOL line is never deployed (LIFE-1). Moving to the next LTS happens within six months of it becoming LTS.

rules.section: 3B · Framework & platform compatibility
rules.title: TypeScript compiles cleanly on the current 6.x without…
rules.text: TypeScript compiles cleanly on the current 6.x without `ignoreDeprecations`, so the move to the native (Go) 7.x compiler is a version bump.

rules.section: 3B · Framework & platform compatibility
rules.title: Tailwind v4 apps take tokens from the kit's CSS-first @theme output
rules.text: Tailwind v4 apps take tokens from the kit's CSS-first `@theme` output (`design/build/tailwind/theme.css`, platform `tailwind4`), never a hand-written theme; the v3 JS preset is only for apps still on v3 (THEME-1).

rules.section: 3B · Framework & platform compatibility
rules.title: Next.js apps follow the current major's conventions
rules.text: Next.js apps follow the current major's conventions (Next 16: `proxy.ts`, async request APIs); upgrades run `@next/codemod` on a branch with the e2e suite green; React Compiler is opted into per app.

rules.section: 3B · Framework & platform compatibility
rules.title: ESLint uses flat config
rules.text: ESLint uses flat config (`eslint.config.*`) only.

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Strict types everywhere
rules.text: **Strict types everywhere:** TS `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, no `any` (use `unknown` + narrowing); Dart `strict-casts`/`strict-inference`/`strict-raw-types`; Python typed and `mypy --strict`/`pyright strict` on new code; Go vet-clean. Typed IDs (`UserId`, not `string`) for anything crossing a boundary.

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Complexity limits, lint-enforced
rules.text: **Complexity limits, lint-enforced:** cyclomatic ≤ 10 per function (≤ 15 with a comment explaining why), cognitive complexity ≤ 15, functions ≤ ~50 lines, files ≤ ~400 lines, ≤ 4 parameters (use an options object), nesting ≤ 3. Exceeding one is a refactor signal, not a target.

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Layering with enforced dependency direction
rules.text: **Layering with enforced dependency direction:** UI → application → domain ← infrastructure. The domain has no framework, DB or HTTP imports; no circular dependencies. Enforced by `dependency-cruiser` (TS), `import-linter` (Python), `go-arch-lint`/`depguard` (Go), `custom_lint`/import rules (Dart).

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Names say what, not how
rules.text: **Names say what, not how:** functions are verbs, booleans read as predicates (`isExpired`, `hasAccess`), no abbreviations beyond the domain's own, units in names where ambiguous (`timeoutMs`). One concept, one name across the codebase (and the same name in the UI and help).

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: No dead weight
rules.text: **No dead weight:** no commented-out code, no unused exports/deps (`knip`, `deadcode`, `vulture`, `dart fix`), no `TODO` without an issue link and owner, no speculative parameters or abstractions with one implementation. A deliberate shortcut is recorded where it lives, in the language's comment syntax, as `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade> (#issue, @owner)` — a TODO with its reason — and `grep -rn "shortcut:"` is the debt ledger reviewed each release. A shortcut never covers a MUST rule of the repo's mode; that is an exception in `docs/STANDARD_EXCEPTIONS.md` (ENF-2).

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Least code that fully does the task
rules.text: **Least code that fully does the task**: in order, ask whether it is needed at all → reuse what the codebase has (the CORE modules first) → the platform / standard library → a dependency already installed → a one-liner → the minimum new code — which, for the second caller of a cross-cutting concern, is the core module (SHR-1). Never add a dependency for what ~20 lines would do (CLEAN-10). **Least never means incomplete:** the change still reaches every caller, and everything the repo's mode requires ships with it — validation, error handling, security, accessibility, the mode's tests (TEST-14 or TEST-0), and in client mode help, `record()` and docs. Deletion beats addition. *(source: ponytail)*

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Errors are explicit
rules.text: **Errors are explicit:** expected failures are typed results or typed errors (CORE-7), not exceptions for control flow; every error carries context on the way up (`fmt.Errorf("load invoice %s: %w", id, err)`); no catch-and-ignore (COR-3).

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Immutability and pure functions by default
rules.text: **Immutability and pure functions by default:** domain logic is pure and data is immutable (`final`, `readonly`, frozen dataclasses); side effects live at the edges where they are easy to test and log.

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Comments explain why, not what;
rules.text: **Comments explain why, not what;** public functions/types of shared modules have doc comments with an example; an ADR records any decision that constrains future work.

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Small, reviewable changes
rules.text: **Small, reviewable changes:** PRs ≤ ~400 changed lines of non-generated **production** code, one concern each; the feature's tests and help/docs (TEST-0, HELP-6) belong in the same PR and don't count toward the limit — split the feature, never its tests; generated files and lockfiles reviewed separately. Every PR states which standard rules it touches and links tests (PR template).

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Adding a dependency is a decision
rules.text: **Adding a dependency is a decision:** check it is maintained (release in the last year), widely used, licence-compatible (REPO-4), small, and not replaceable by ~20 lines of code or the platform; record why in the PR. Dependencies are updated on a schedule (Renovate, grouped, weekly) — not in a yearly panic.

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Formatting is automatic and non-negotiable
rules.text: **Formatting is automatic and non-negotiable** (`gofmt`, `prettier`, `dart format`, `ruff format`, `swift-format`); no style debates in review.

rules.section: 3A · Clean code & maintainability
rules.title: Review checklist
rules.text: **Review checklist** (in the PR template): correctness and edge cases · authz on every new path · input validation · logging/audit via the core · tests of all four kinds · help/docs · performance of new queries · no new dependency without CLEAN-10 · no secrets · standard rule IDs.

rules.section: 4 · Correctness & honesty
rules.title: Never fabricate success
rules.text: **Never fabricate success.** If code cannot perform an action (no driver, no credential, no backend) it returns an explicit error — never a plausible "ok". Mocks/simulators are impossible to select in production builds.

rules.section: 4 · Correctness & honesty
rules.title: Demo/seed data is gated behind an explicit flag, visibly labelled in…
rules.text: Demo/seed data is gated behind an explicit flag, visibly labelled in the UI, and never mixed into real aggregates.

rules.section: 4 · Correctness & honesty
rules.title: No silent catch {} / ignored errors
rules.text: No silent `catch {}` / ignored errors. Every catch logs (LOG-*) or rethrows with context.

rules.section: 4 · Correctness & honesty
rules.title: Multi-step writes are transactional
rules.text: Multi-step writes are transactional; deletes are intentional (cascade vs soft) and documented.

rules.section: 4 · Correctness & honesty
rules.title: Everything wired is reachable
rules.text: Everything wired is reachable: routes registered, workers started at boot, endpoints called by something. Unreachable code is deleted, not kept "for later".

rules.section: 4 · Correctness & honesty
rules.title: Every user-tunable runtime parameter has a UI
rules.text: Every user-tunable runtime parameter has a UI (or is documented as deploy-only).

rules.section: 4 · Correctness & honesty
rules.title: Migrations are forward-only-safe with a tested way back
rules.text: Migrations are forward-only-safe with a tested way back — a down migration, or (with expand → contract) proof that the previous release runs on the new schema, so rolling back the app alone is the rollback; dry-run in a transaction with `ON_ERROR_STOP` before prod. Event/API payloads are versioned. Migrations are safe on a live database: renames and drops go expand → migrate → contract across releases; indexes on existing tables are built `CONCURRENTLY`, as the only statement in a migration that runs outside a transaction (dry-run against a copy instead); a `lock_timeout` is set; a new `NOT NULL` column has a default; schema (DDL) and data backfills are separate migrations; a migration that has run anywhere shared is never edited — a new one corrects it. *Enforced by:* `squawk` (Postgres) or `atlas migrate lint` in CI. *(source: ecc-database-migrations)*
enforcedBy: doc:`squawk` (Postgres) or `atlas migrate lint` in CI. (source: ecc-database-migrations)

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.subsection: LOG-1 · The event schema (MUST — OpenTelemetry log data model + semantic conventions)
rules.title: The event schema
rules.text: The event schema (MUST — OpenTelemetry log data model + semantic conventions) Every log record follows the **OTel log data model** and uses **OTel semantic-convention attribute names**, so logs, traces and metrics join up in any OTel backend (App Insights, Grafana, Datadog, Honeycomb) without remapping. App-specific attributes live under the `app.` namespace. On the wire (JSON), keys are the dotted names below.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: All logging goes through CORE-3. Recommended implementations
rules.text: All logging goes through CORE-3. Recommended implementations: Go `log/slog` (JSON handler) · Node `pino` · Python `structlog` (or stdlib + JSON formatter) · Swift `os.Logger` + remote sink · Flutter/Dart `package:logging` → backend sink · traces/metrics via **OpenTelemetry** SDK, exported over OTLP.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Level discipline
rules.text: Level discipline: `error` = someone should look — it counts toward error-rate / burn-rate alerts (REL-1), never pages on a single occurrence; `warn` = degraded but handled; `info` = business events and request summaries; `debug` = off in prod by default, switchable at runtime without redeploy.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Redaction at the logger
rules.text: **Redaction at the logger**, not the call site: a denylist of keys (`password|secret|token|authorization|cookie|api[_-]?key|ssn|card`) plus value-pattern scrubbing (JWTs, bearer tokens, long hex/base64). PII is hashed or omitted, except the LOG-1 identity and HTTP fields (`user.id`, `client.address`, `user_agent.original`), which are kept (IP truncated where DATA_INVENTORY says so). Unit-test the redactor.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Audit rides on logging
rules.text: **Audit rides on logging.** `record()` (CORE-4) emits one event that lands in (a) the app log, (b) the **append-only** audit store for every state change and privileged read, and (c) the user-visible activity feed where relevant. Audit records carry who/what/when/from-where (IP, user-agent)/outcome and are immutable to the app (DB role without UPDATE/DELETE; optional hash chain). **Erasure vs immutability:** audit records are kept for their LOG-9 retention under the legal basis recorded in DATA_INVENTORY, identify the actor by an internal ID (never email/name), and are not rewritten when an account is deleted (STORE-4, PRIV-3); deleting the account removes the ID → person mapping, and the privacy notice says audit records age out at their retention.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Producer coverage
rules.text: **Producer coverage**: every subsystem that mutates state calls `record()`. A dashboard or audit log fed by 9 of 63 subsystems is worse than none. Keep a producer × sink table in `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Every request emits exactly one summary record
rules.text: Every request emits exactly one summary record (`event.name: http.request` with `http.request.method`, `http.route`, `http.response.status_code`, `app.duration_ms`) plus spans for downstream calls, and the `http.server.request.duration` metric.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Client apps
rules.text: Client apps: crash reporter live with release tag and uploaded symbols; client errors carry `request_id`; no raw `print`/`console` in release builds.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Logs are centralized, retained per policy
rules.text: Logs are centralized, retained per policy (default 30 d app / 1 y audit), access- controlled, and alerting exists for: error-rate spike (as burn-rate alerts, REL-1), auth-failure spike, job not run on schedule, audit-write failure.

rules.section: 5 · Unified logging, audit & telemetry
rules.title: Golden signals per service as metrics
rules.text: Golden signals per service as metrics (latency, traffic, errors, saturation) with one dashboard; job freshness (`last_success_ts`) exported per job.

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: Every screen uses CORE-11 page chrome and implements all four states
rules.text: Every screen uses CORE-11 page chrome and implements all four states: loading, empty, error (actionable, shows `request_id`), data.

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: All colour, type, spacing, radius, elevation and icons come from…
rules.text: All colour, type, spacing, radius, elevation and icons come from CORE-13 per §6A.

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: Lists
rules.text: Lists: drill-down to the item, filter, sort, paginate, **export** (CSV/JSON) — free via the shared grid.

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: Inputs that reference existing objects are pickers bound to real…
rules.text: Inputs that reference existing objects are **pickers bound to real data**, not free text.

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: WCAG 2.2 AA: labels on icon buttons, contrast in both themes,…
rules.text: WCAG 2.2 AA: labels on icon buttons, contrast in both themes, keyboard navigation, focus visible, tap targets ≥ 44pt / 48dp, text scales to 200% without clipping.

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: One formatting helper each for money, numbers, dates
rules.text: One formatting helper each for money, numbers, dates (locale from data); strings externalized for i18n; `mailto:` built with RFC 3986 encoding (`%20`, not `+`).

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: Every screen and field has in-app help and a living-docs page per §6G
rules.text: Every screen and field has in-app help and a living-docs page per §6G.

rules.section: 6 · UX consistency, accessibility, docs
rules.title: Network resilience
rules.text: Network resilience: offline/slow/5xx states are graceful; token expiry triggers silent refresh via the refresh token (never an IdP `prompt=none` session, SESS-5); reconnect backfills missed realtime state.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Each app has exactly one token source, authored in the W3C Design Tokens
rules.text: Each app has exactly **one** token source, authored in the W3C **Design Tokens** (DTCG) JSON format and generated for its platform(s) by the kit's zero-dependency `tools/standard/design-tokens/scripts/build.mjs` (CSS vars, Tailwind v4 `@theme` CSS per COMPAT-4 — the v3 JS preset only for apps still on v3 — TS, Flutter `ThemeExtension`, SwiftUI). DTCG keeps the source compatible with Style Dictionary and Tokens Studio (Figma) if a designer joins. A web + mobile app generates both from the same source, so they match. Generated files are never hand-edited. Two theme/colour files in one app (e.g. `theme_colors.dart` *and* `app_colors.dart`) is a finding.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Two tiers
rules.text: Two tiers: **primitive** tokens (this app's palette, scale) and **semantic** tokens (`color.bg.surface`, `color.text.muted`, `color.status.danger`, `color.border.focus`, `color.action.primary`). App code references **semantic tokens only**. Light, dark and each preset are different semantic maps over the same keys.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Consistency within the app
rules.text: **Consistency within the app:** a meaning maps to one token everywhere — the same "danger", "success", "selected", "disabled", "link" on every screen, chart and badge. Domain colours (e.g. per category, per segment, per player) are semantic tokens too (`color.category.music`), defined once, never re-picked per screen.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Shared semantic vocabulary across apps
rules.text: **Shared semantic vocabulary across apps:** every app uses the *same token names* (its values are its own). This keeps the lint rules, the review harness and the contrast checker identical everywhere, and lets a developer move between apps without relearning. The canonical key and icon list is `engineering-standard/design-tokens/schema/semantic-keys.json`; apps may add keys under `color.domain.*` / `icon.domain.*`, never rename. `validate.mjs` enforces this.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Icons through a registry
rules.text: **Icons through a registry:** the app picks **one** icon set per platform (e.g. Lucide, Material Symbols, SF Symbols) and exposes semantic names (`action.delete`, `action.edit`, `nav.settings`, `status.warning`). Screens use the registry, never the icon package directly — so "delete" is the same glyph, size and colour token everywhere. Icon sizes are tokens (`icon.sm|md|lg`). App icon, splash and favicon are generated from one source per app.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Theme mode = system | light | dark
rules.text: Theme mode = `system | light | dark` (+ the app's presets if offered), held by one theme controller (CORE-13), applied before first render (no flash), switchable at runtime without restart. Every screen works in both light and dark from the first commit. In client mode the choice is persisted **per user** in the backend profile (local cache for first paint); in quick mode following the OS setting is enough.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Contrast is validated at token build time: every text/background…
rules.text: Contrast is validated **at token build time**: every text/background semantic pair meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text/UI) in every mode and preset; the build fails otherwise.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: No raw colours, font sizes, spacing values or direct icon-package…
rules.text: No raw colours, font sizes, spacing values or direct icon-package imports in screen code (lint, §7.2). Third-party components are themed through an adapter that maps them to tokens — including a dark bridge.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Visual regression in both modes: golden tests
rules.text: Visual regression in **both modes**: golden tests (Flutter) / Playwright screenshots (web) for a smoke set of screens per mode and preset, in CI.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion and breakpoints are…
rules.text: Typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion and breakpoints are tokens too.

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: Design skills work inside the token system
rules.text: **Design skills work inside the token system.** A design-generation skill (e.g. Anthropic's `frontend-design`, a pinned companion — `sources/registry.json`) treats this section as the brief: its palette/typography step proposes primitive values and semantic mappings for the THEME-4 keys in `design/tokens/*.json` (THEME-2; new keys only under `color.domain.*`), AA-validated in every mode and preset (THEME-7); generated screens use only semantic tokens and the icon registry — no hex/rgb, palette classes, size or spacing literals (THEME-8); every new screen works in light and dark (THEME-6). In client mode also: fonts at most two families, self-hosted WOFF2 (PERF-16), and every screen has its four states (UX-1). Its taste guidance (avoiding generic AI looks, hierarchy, copy) applies within that — in both modes. *(source: anthropic-frontend-design)*

rules.section: 6A · Design system & theming — central management *per app*
rules.title: A living reference page per app
rules.text: A living reference page per app (Storybook / Widgetbook / a `/design` route in dev builds) renders every token, icon and shared component in every mode.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: The API contract is a checked-in schema
rules.text: The API contract is a checked-in schema (OpenAPI 3.1 / GraphQL SDL / protobuf / typed RPC) that is the source of truth; clients and validators are generated from it, and CI fails on drift.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Versioned routes or additive-only changes
rules.text: Versioned routes or additive-only changes; breaking changes need a new version and a deprecation window long enough for shipped mobile clients.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Every mutating endpoint that can be retried accepts an idempotency key
rules.text: Every mutating endpoint that can be retried accepts an **idempotency key**.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Rate limiting and quotas on every public endpoint
rules.text: **Rate limiting and quotas on every public endpoint** (per user, per IP, per tenant), stricter on auth, signup, password reset, OTP, file upload and anything that costs money (LLM, SMS).

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: One error format everywhere
rules.text: One error format everywhere (CORE-7; CORE-12 parses it): **RFC 9457 Problem Details** (`Content-Type: application/problem+json`) — `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance`, plus extension members `code` (stable CORE-7 code) and `request_id`; field errors in an `errors` array (`{pointer, code, detail}`). Never leak stack traces or SQL.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Resource-oriented naming
rules.text: **Resource-oriented naming:** plural nouns (`/invoices/{id}`), lower-case kebab paths, one JSON casing per API, timestamps RFC 3339 UTC, money as integer minor units + ISO 4217 currency, IDs opaque strings.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Pagination
rules.text: **Pagination** is cursor-based: `page_size` (with a documented max) and `page_token` in; `next_page_token` out (empty when done). No offset pagination on large or changing collections.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Filtering and sorting
rules.text: **Filtering and sorting** use one convention per API (e.g. `filter=` expression and `order_by=field desc`), validated against an allow-list of fields — never passed into a query raw.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Updates
rules.text: **Updates:** `PATCH` with JSON Merge Patch (or an explicit field mask); optimistic concurrency via `ETag` + `If-Match` (412 on conflict) for resources more than one person edits.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Long-running work
rules.text: **Long-running work** returns `202 Accepted` with an operation resource (`/operations/{id}`: status, progress, result or problem) instead of holding the request open.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: Deprecation is signalled in-band
rules.text: **Deprecation is signalled in-band:** `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers (plus a `Link` to the migration note) on deprecated endpoints, at least one mobile release cycle before removal, and not removed while the oldest supported app version (LIFE-3) still calls it.

rules.section: 6B · API contract
rules.title: The OWASP API Security Top 10 is reviewed per API: object-level authz
rules.text: The **OWASP API Security Top 10** is reviewed per API: object-level authz (SEC-7), function-level authz (SEC-6), property-level exposure (explicit response DTOs, no `SELECT *` to JSON), resource consumption limits (API-4, PERF-3), SSRF (SEC-5), and an inventory of every deployed API version (no forgotten `v1`).

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Tokens/keys only in the platform secure store
rules.text: Tokens/keys only in the platform secure store (Keychain / Android Keystore via `flutter_secure_storage` or equivalent) — never SharedPreferences/UserDefaults/localStorage.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: ATS on
rules.text: ATS on (iOS) / `cleartextTrafficPermitted=false` (Android); no debug flags or verbose logging in release; screenshots hidden for sensitive screens where appropriate.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Deep-link and push payloads are validated as untrusted input
rules.text: Deep-link and push payloads are validated as untrusted input (SEC-1) and never carry secrets.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Verified links only
rules.text: **Verified links only:** Android App Links (`assetlinks.json`) and iOS Universal Links (`apple-app-site-association`) for anything that opens the app with state; custom URL schemes never carry auth codes.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: App attestation
rules.text: **App attestation** (Play Integrity / App Attest) on APIs that cost money or expose sensitive data, enforced server-side. Firebase apps: FB-1 makes this a MUST via App Check.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Certificate pinning is a recorded decision
rules.text: **Certificate pinning is a recorded decision** (ADR): default is *no pinning* plus ATS/Network Security Config; if pinned, pin the SPKI with a backup pin and a remote kill switch (CORE-15) so a rotated certificate can't brick the app.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Nothing sensitive in backups, logs, clipboard or screenshots
rules.text: **Nothing sensitive in backups, logs, clipboard or screenshots:** tokens and PII excluded from device/cloud backup (Android `dataExtractionRules`; iOS Keychain `ThisDeviceOnly` + `isExcludedFromBackup`), sensitive non-password fields mark `secureTextEntry`/disable autofill, suggestions and autocorrect (password fields keep password-manager autofill, AUTH-3), secrets are never copied to the clipboard by the app, app switcher snapshot blurred on sensitive screens.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Store privacy declarations match the code
rules.text: **Store privacy declarations match the code:** Apple privacy manifest (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, required-reason APIs) and Google Play Data safety form are updated in the same PR as any new SDK or data collection.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Release builds are obfuscated
rules.text: Release builds are obfuscated (`--obfuscate --split-debug-info`, R8) with symbols uploaded privately; MASVS-RESILIENCE controls (root/jailbreak detection) only where the threat model calls for them.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Biometric unlock releases a key, not a boolean
rules.text: **Biometric unlock releases a key, not a boolean:** biometrics gate a Keychain / Android Keystore key that requires user authentication and is invalidated when biometric enrolment changes; a bare `local_auth` / `LAContext` success result never decides access on its own.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: Every Android component sets android:exported explicitly
rules.text: Every Android component sets `android:exported` explicitly; only the launcher, App Links activities and components that must be reachable from other apps are exported, and those validate their input (MOB-3). *Enforced by:* merged-manifest allow-list in CI.

rules.section: 6C · Mobile & client security
rules.title: WebView / hybrid hardening
rules.text: **WebView / hybrid hardening:** no WebView remote debugging in release builds, no navigation wildcards, JavaScript bridges exposed only to the app's own origin; Capacitor `server.url`, `cleartext` and `allowMixedContent` are off in production builds **unless an ADR records a remote-shell design** (then the ADR lists the compensating controls and the origin allow-list).

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: Release builds meet the current store floors
rules.text: Release builds meet the current store floors: Android `targetSdk` **36** (required for updates since 2026-08-31); iOS built with **Xcode 26 / the iOS 26 SDK** (required since 2026-04-28). Set `targetSdk` explicitly rather than inheriting a framework default. *Enforced by:* `aapt2 dump badging` ≥ 36 and the `DTSDKName` of the archive in CI.
enforcedBy: doc:`aapt2 dump badging` ≥ 36 and the `DTSDKName` of the archive in CI.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: Every native .so in an Android release is 16 KB page-aligned
rules.text: Every native `.so` in an Android release is **16 KB page-aligned** (Play blocks non-compliant updates from 2027-02-01; AGP ≥ 8.5.1, NDK r28+). Plugins with native code (ML Kit / `mobile_scanner`, `sqlite3`) are where it breaks. *Enforced by:* `zipalign -c -P 16` and an ELF alignment check on the release artifact.
enforcedBy: doc:`zipalign -c -P 16` and an ELF alignment check on the release artifact.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: Android 16 readiness
rules.text: **Android 16 readiness** at API 36: no edge-to-edge opt-out; predictive back (`PopScope`, never `WillPopScope`); orientation and resizability locks are ignored on screens ≥ 600dp, so layouts work there. THEME-9 goldens add a 600dp landscape size with system insets.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: Account deletion
rules.text: **Account deletion** is available in the app (Apple 5.1.1(v)) **and** from a web URL listed in Play Console, and deletes the user's server data in every user-owned table and storage bucket (audit records per LOG-5, processors per PRIV-3). *Test:* pgTAP/integration test finds zero user rows outside the LOG-5 audit store after deletion; CI requests the web URL.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: An app that offers Google
rules.text: An app that offers Google (or other third-party) sign-in also offers an equivalent privacy-preserving login (Apple 4.8; Sign in with Apple satisfies it).

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: Apps available in Texas
rules.text: *Apps available in Texas* (SB 2420, enforceable since 2026): age assurance from the store's age signal (Apple Declared Age Range, Play Age Signals), parental consent refreshed on a significant change, and age data deleted after use. Other jurisdictions' age-assurance laws are tracked per app in an ADR (**SHOULD** until each one's date is confirmed).

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: No READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/READ_MEDIA_VIDEO unless media access is the…
rules.text: No `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`/`READ_MEDIA_VIDEO` unless media access is the app's core purpose (use the system photo picker); every foreground service declares its type and permission; exact alarms only for alarm/calendar apps. *Enforced by:* merged-manifest permission allow-list.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: Staged rollouts halt when Android vitals cross Play's bad-behaviour…
rules.text: Staged rollouts halt when Android vitals cross Play's bad-behaviour thresholds (user-perceived crash rate 1.09%, ANR rate 0.47% overall; 8% on any single device model). *Enforced by:* a Play Reporting API check before raising the rollout percentage.
enforcedBy: doc:a Play Reporting API check before raising the rollout percentage.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: --dart-define, --dart-define-from-file and env.json hold public…
rules.text: `--dart-define`, `--dart-define-from-file` and `env*.json` hold **public config only** — their values are compiled into the binary and obfuscation doesn't hide them (SEC-11). *Enforced by:* `strings` over `libapp.so` / `App.framework` for `sb_secret_`, `service_role`, `PRIVATE KEY`, `sk-`; gitleaks over `env*.json`.
enforcedBy: doc:`strings` over `libapp.so` / `App.framework` for `sbsecret`, `servicerole`, `PRIVATE KEY`, `sk-`; gitleaks over `env.json`.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: iOS/macOS builds use Swift Package Manager
rules.text: iOS/macOS builds use Swift Package Manager (CocoaPods trunk becomes read-only 2026-12-02); `enable-swift-package-manager: false` is never set.

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: pubspec.lock is committed
rules.text: `pubspec.lock` is committed (apps) and scanned on a schedule (`osv-scanner -L pubspec.lock`, `dart pub outdated` weekly — VULN-3).

rules.section: 6J · App stores & Flutter
rules.title: CI pins the Flutter version
rules.text: CI pins the Flutter version (`.fvmrc` or the workflow) and upgrades deliberately.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Authorization runs in the data-access layer, in every Server Action…
rules.text: Authorization runs in the data-access layer, in **every Server Action and every `route.ts`** — never only in `middleware.ts`/`proxy.ts`, which has been bypassed (CVE-2025-29927). *Enforced by:* semgrep — a `'use server'` export or route handler that reaches the DB without the CORE-5 check first.
enforcedBy: doc:semgrep — a `'use server'` export or route handler that reaches the DB without the CORE-5 check first.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Every Server Action is a public POST endpoint: schema-validated…
rules.text: Every Server Action is a **public POST endpoint**: schema-validated arguments (CORE-9), an ownership check (SEC-7), and a minimal DTO in return — never a raw ORM record.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Modules that touch secrets, the database or server-only process.env…
rules.text: Modules that touch secrets, the database or server-only `process.env` start with `import 'server-only'`; `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables hold no secret. *Test:* grep `.next/static` for secret names.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Next.js stays on a supported release line and takes each Next.js…
rules.text: Next.js stays on a supported release line and takes each Next.js security release within the VULN-2 deadline for its severity (React Server Components flaws such as CVE-2025-55182 are Critical); `next` is pinned to an exact version, since it bundles its React server packages. *Enforced by:* a CI version-floor assertion + `osv-scanner`.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: images.remotePatterns lists exact protocol, hostname and path prefix
rules.text: `images.remotePatterns` lists exact protocol, hostname and path prefix — no wildcards; `dangerouslyAllowSVG` stays off; rewrites and redirects never build a destination host from request input (SSRF, SEC-5).

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Cached code
rules.text: Cached code (`'use cache'`, Cache Components, `unstable_cache`) never reads cookies, headers or the session, and never returns per-user data unless the user is part of the cache key (PERF-27). *Test:* e2e as user A then user B — B sees none of A's data.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: No request data in server module scope
rules.text: **No request data in server module scope.** Server components, route handlers and Server Actions keep request- and user-scoped data in function scope (or per-request memoisation such as `React.cache` / request context — not a NEXT-6 cache), never in mutable module-level variables — concurrent renders share the module and can serve one user's data to another (PERF-27). *Enforced by:* the kit's `std.web.server-module-state` semgrep rule + review lens. *(source: vercel-react-best-practices)*
enforcedBy: doc:the kit's `std.web.server-module-state` semgrep rule + review lens. (source: vercel-react-best-practices)

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Clients use publishable keys
rules.text: Clients use **publishable** keys (`sb_publishable_…`); **secret** keys (`sb_secret_…`) live only in servers and Edge Functions; the legacy `anon`/`service_role` JWT keys are disabled before Supabase removes them (end of 2026). `verify_jwt` doesn't authenticate a caller that sends only an API key, so every Edge Function authorizes in code. *Test:* call each function with only the publishable key → 401/403.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: supabase db advisors
rules.text: `supabase db advisors` (security + performance lints) runs in CI and fails on ERROR: RLS disabled, `SECURITY DEFINER` views, definer functions callable by `anon`, listable public buckets, always-true policies.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Supabase authorization traps
rules.text: **Supabase authorization traps.** No policy or function authorizes from `user_metadata` / `raw_user_meta_data` (users can edit it, and it appears in `auth.jwt()`); every UPDATE policy has both `USING` and `WITH CHECK`; on user- or tenant-owned rows `TO authenticated` is paired with an ownership predicate (alone it is authentication, not authorization), and a policy deliberately open to every signed-in user says so in a comment; `SECURITY DEFINER` functions live outside exposed schemas or have `EXECUTE` revoked from `PUBLIC` and `anon`; the CLI, CI, MCP servers and agents use scoped personal access tokens, never a full-account token; deleting a user revokes their sessions first (access tokens outlive the user). *Test:* a migration lint for `user_metadata` and for UPDATE policies without `WITH CHECK`; pgTAP for cross-user update and post-deletion access. *(source: supabase-agent-skill)*

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: RLS policies
rules.text: RLS policies (SEC-8) are written for performance too: `(select auth.uid())` rather than `auth.uid()`, a `TO authenticated` role clause, and an index on every column a policy filters on; views use `security_invoker = true`; definer functions set `search_path = ''`.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Leaked-password protection is on, and Auth settings are diffed…
rules.text: Leaked-password protection is on, and Auth settings are diffed against a committed copy via the Management API.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Firebase App Check
rules.text: **Firebase App Check** is enforced for each Firebase product once its metrics show valid tokens; iOS uses App Attest, and the debug provider is compiled in only under `kDebugMode`. (Firebase apps' form of MOB-5.)

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Firebase Analytics collection is off until the user consents
rules.text: Firebase Analytics collection is off until the user consents (`FIREBASE_ANALYTICS_COLLECTION_ENABLED=false`, then `setConsent` / enable on consent); push is sent through the FCM HTTP v1 API only.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Firestore and Storage rules are tested as code
rules.text: **Firestore and Storage rules are tested as code.** Rules take authority (`role`, `isAdmin`, `ownerId`) only from `request.auth` or server-written documents, never from `request.resource.data`; `update` is at least as strict as `create`, so a document can't be created valid and then updated into an escalated state; every written field is type-checked and size-limited; `hasOnly()` / `diff()` are always paired with an ownership check. Emulator tests (`@firebase/rules-unit-testing`) cover, per collection and Storage path, the denied path and a create-then-escalate attempt (TEST-2). *(source: firebase-rules-auditor)*

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Key Vaults use Azure RBAC
rules.text: Key Vaults use Azure RBAC (not access policies) with purge protection on.

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Azure Files shares holding irreplaceable data have share soft-delete…
rules.text: Azure Files shares holding irreplaceable data have share soft-delete **and** snapshots or Azure Backup — snapshots are deleted with the share (OPS-3).

rules.section: 6K · Backend platforms — Next.js, Supabase, Firebase, Azure
rules.title: Defender for Cloud Foundational CSPM
rules.text: Defender for Cloud Foundational CSPM (free) is on and Secure Score is reviewed monthly.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: (client mode
rules.text: *(client mode; quick mode uses TEST-14)* Every new or changed feature/screen ships with **four kinds of test** in the same PR: | Kind | Proves | Typical tooling | |---|---|---| | **Unit** | Its logic, validation, formatting, state transitions — including edge cases (0 / 1 / max, invalid input) | `go test`, `vitest`/`jest`, `pytest`, `flutter test`, XCTest | | **Integration** | Each API/mutation against a real DB/emulator: happy path **and the denied path** (wrong role, other user's/tenant's record), transaction rollback, audit event written | testcontainers, Supabase local, Firebase emulator | | **E2E journey** | The main task end to end through the real UI, per role (e.g. member creates → admin approves) | Playwright, Flutter `integration_test`, XCUITest | | **Walkthrough** | The Day-1 walk of the screen (APP_REVIEW §4), automated — see TEST-6 | same as e2e |

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Pyramid
rules.text: Pyramid: many unit, fewer integration, fewest e2e/walkthrough. No production data in fixtures — use factories and a seeded test tenant.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Every mutation has a test for the denied path as well as the happy path
rules.text: Every mutation has a test for the **denied** path as well as the happy path.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Coverage floor on platform-core modules
rules.text: Coverage floor on platform-core modules (≥ 80% lines) and on **changed lines** in a PR (≥ 70%); no repo-wide vanity target. Coverage counts behaviour, not snapshot-only render tests.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: E2E/walkthrough runs authenticated
rules.text: E2E/walkthrough runs **authenticated** (asserts it is not on `/login`), in **both themes**, and fails on console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed network requests — except requests the test itself fails on purpose (e.g. to render the TEST-6 error state), which it declares.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Flaky tests are quarantined, not retried until green
rules.text: Flaky tests are quarantined, not retried until green. Quarantine is the **only** permitted way to skip a test: the skip carries `quarantine`, an owner and an ISO date in its reason, it lands in its own PR (never in the change that makes other tests pass, AGT-8), and it is fixed or deleted by that date. Emergency patches (VULN-5) still run every non-quarantined test.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Walkthrough test per screen
rules.text: **Walkthrough test per screen** — one spec per routable screen that performs, in order: open it as a fresh user → assert loading, **empty**, error and data states render → configure / create an object through the UI → see it populate → drill into it → edit and delete it → export → open help (HELP-1) → verify an audit event with actor + role was written (LOG-5) → screenshot in light and dark (THEME-9) → repeat as a lower role and assert the denied paths. The same specs regenerate help screenshots (HELP-10) and are the live evidence for `APP_REVIEW.md`.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Feature → test map is enforced
rules.text: **Feature → test map is enforced:** every feature key in the nav/router inventory has tests tagged with it (`@feature:<key>` in the test name or tag) covering all four TEST-0 kinds — unit, integration, e2e and walkthrough (`bin/check-tests.mjs`; a feature with no server side records `integration` under `allowMissing` with a reason); a CI step lists features missing any kind and fails. A new route without tagged tests cannot merge.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Bugs get a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after
rules.text: Bugs get a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after (proven per TEST-15), in the same PR.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Every new test is proven able to fail
rules.text: **Every new test is proven able to fail.** For new logic and every bug fix, write the test first and see it fail for the expected reason, then write the code (red → green → refactor) — the preferred order. If the code came first: revert the change, see the test fail for the expected reason, restore it, see it pass. A test not proven able to fail doesn't count toward TEST-14 / TEST-0. Either way the red run counts only if it fails **at an assertion** — a compile, import or setup failure, or a whole-test timeout, proves nothing (an assertion's own retry timeout, e.g. `expect(locator).toBeVisible()`, is an assertion failure) — and its output shows that assertion. *(sources: superpowers, anthropic-code-modernization)*

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Fuzz anything that parses untrusted input
rules.text: **Fuzz anything that parses untrusted input** (file formats, decoders, URL/filter parsers, import code): Go native fuzzing, Atheris (Python), Jazzer.js; fuzz targets run in CI for a short budget and nightly for longer; crashes become regression tests (TEST-8).

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Property-based tests
rules.text: **Property-based tests** for domain invariants (money never negative, totals equal the sum of lines, round-trip encode/decode): `fast-check`, `hypothesis`, `rapid`/`gopter`, `glados` (Dart).

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Mutation testing
rules.text: **Mutation testing** on platform-core and domain modules each quarter (Stryker, `mutmut`, `go-mutesting`); a mutation score under ~70% means the tests run the code without checking it.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Automated accessibility checks
rules.text: **Automated accessibility checks** in CI: `@axe-core/playwright` on every walkthrough page (web), Flutter `meetsGuideline` (tap targets, contrast, labels) in widget tests — zero serious violations.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: (quick mode
rules.text: *(quick mode — §0A)* Every new or changed feature ships in the same PR with **unit tests** for its logic (edge cases included) and **one e2e test of its main journey**, tagged `@feature:<key>`; TEST-2 (denied path), TEST-5 (quarantine) and TEST-8 (regression test per bug) still apply. `bin/check-tests.mjs` requires `unit` + `e2e` in quick mode. TEST-0 replaces this rule when the repo moves to client mode.

rules.section: 6D · Testing standard — tests are part of the feature
rules.title: Contract tests between client and API are generated from the API-1…
rules.text: Contract tests between client and API are generated from the API-1 schema; load smoke (`k6`) at expected peak for APIs with a PERF-1 budget; visual-regression goldens for the shared components.

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: /healthz
rules.text: `/healthz` (liveness) and `/readyz` (dependencies) endpoints; graceful shutdown that drains in-flight requests and jobs.

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: CI/CD: gates
rules.text: CI/CD: gates (§7.1) → preview/staging deploy → migrations → prod, with a one-command **rollback** that has been exercised. Deploys are tagged with the git SHA logged as `service.version` (LOG-1).

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: Backups with written RPO/RTO; a restore is actually performed and…
rules.text: Backups with written **RPO/RTO**; a restore is actually performed and verified at least quarterly (a backup never restored is a hope).

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: Environments are config-identical except for values
rules.text: Environments are config-identical except for values; secrets differ per environment; prod data never copied to dev unmasked.

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: A docs/RUNBOOK.md
rules.text: A `docs/RUNBOOK.md`: how to deploy, roll back, rotate each secret, restore, and respond to each alert in LOG-9.

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: Cost guardrails
rules.text: Cost guardrails: budget alerts on cloud/LLM/SMS spend; per-tenant usage metered.

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: Uptime monitoring
rules.text: Uptime monitoring (e.g. Uptime Kuma) on every public endpoint and TLS expiry.

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: Stateless, disposable processes
rules.text: **Stateless, disposable processes** (Twelve-Factor): no state on local disk or in process memory that another replica needs; start in seconds, shut down gracefully (OPS-1), so any instance can be killed or scaled at any time. Dev, staging and prod use the same backing-service types (no SQLite-in-dev / Postgres-in-prod).

rules.section: 6E · Operations & delivery
rules.title: DORA metrics
rules.text: **DORA metrics** tracked monthly per app — deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore — to see whether the standard is making delivery faster and safer, not slower.

rules.section: 6H · Reliability & incidents
rules.title: SLOs per user-facing service
rules.text: **SLOs per user-facing service:** 2–4 SLIs that reflect user experience (availability of key journeys, p95 latency, freshness of background data) with targets (e.g. 99.5% monthly) written in `docs/SLO.md`. Alerts (LOG-9) fire on **error-budget burn rate**, not on single errors.

rules.section: 6H · Reliability & incidents
rules.title: Error budget policy
rules.text: **Error budget policy:** when a service has spent its monthly budget, reliability work takes priority over features until it recovers.

rules.section: 6H · Reliability & incidents
rules.title: Incident process
rules.text: **Incident process** in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`: severities (SEV1 user-facing outage or data/ security incident · SEV2 degraded · SEV3 minor), who is notified and how, a single incident lead, a status note for users for SEV1/2, and the first steps for each alert.

rules.section: 6H · Reliability & incidents
rules.title: Blameless postmortem
rules.text: **Blameless postmortem** within 5 business days for every SEV1/SEV2 and every security incident: timeline, impact, root causes (plural), what went well, action items with owners and dates tracked as issues. Repeated causes become standard rules or lint checks.

rules.section: 6H · Reliability & incidents
rules.title: Disaster recovery is rehearsed
rules.text: **Disaster recovery is rehearsed:** RPO/RTO per data store (OPS-3), a full DR rehearsal into a clean environment at least twice a year (in addition to OPS-3's quarterly restore test), and a written, tested procedure for losing the primary region/host (for a single-VM host: rebuild from IaC + backups, timed).

rules.section: 6H · Reliability & incidents
rules.title: Resilience is tested, not assumed
rules.text: **Resilience is tested, not assumed:** each critical dependency (DB, auth provider, payment, LLM, email) has a tested failure mode — timeouts, fallback or a clear degraded UI — exercised by fault-injection tests or a game day.

rules.section: 6H · Reliability & incidents
rules.title: Graceful degradation
rules.text: **Graceful degradation:** a failing non-critical dependency (analytics, recommendations, avatars) never takes down a critical journey; bulkheads separate their timeouts and pools.

rules.section: 6I · Vulnerability management & disclosure
rules.title: Every repo has a SECURITY.md
rules.text: Every repo has a `SECURITY.md` (kit template) stating how to report a vulnerability, the response time, and supported versions; every website publishes `/.well-known/security.txt` (WEB-9). Public GitHub repos enable private vulnerability reporting (GitHub offers it only for public repos).

rules.section: 6I · Vulnerability management & disclosure
rules.title: Fix-time targets from discovery
rules.text: **Fix-time targets from discovery** (scanner, report, or advisory): **Critical 7 days · High 30 days · Medium 90 days · Low next planned release.** Actively exploited (CISA KEV) = Critical regardless of score. Overdue items are reported weekly until closed.

rules.section: 6I · Vulnerability management & disclosure
rules.title: Continuous monitoring of what is already shipped
rules.text: **Continuous monitoring of what is already shipped:** Dependabot/Renovate security alerts on, and a scheduled scan (weekly) of the default branch and the latest release with `osv-scanner` / `govulncheck` — a CVE published after release still has to be found.

rules.section: 6I · Vulnerability management & disclosure
rules.title: Triage is recorded
rules.text: **Triage is recorded:** each finding is fixed, or marked not-affected with a reason (VEX-style statement in the issue or `docs/STANDARD_EXCEPTIONS.md`) — never silently ignored.

rules.section: 6I · Vulnerability management & disclosure
rules.title: Emergency patch path
rules.text: **Emergency patch path:** a documented way to ship a security fix to production within hours (skipping non-essential gates, never skipping tests), plus forced-update / kill switch for mobile (CORE-15).

rules.section: 6I · Vulnerability management & disclosure
rules.title: Repo security posture is measured
rules.text: **Repo security posture is measured:** the OpenSSF **Scorecard** action (kit template) runs weekly on every GitHub repo (private repos need a read-only `SCORECARD_TOKEN` secret); target score ≥ 7/10, and a drop is investigated.

rules.section: 6I · Vulnerability management & disclosure
rules.title: Security fixes are disclosed honestly in the CHANGELOG / release…
rules.text: Security fixes are disclosed honestly in the CHANGELOG / release notes once users can update (CVE or advisory where applicable).

rules.section: 6F · Repo hygiene
rules.title: README
rules.text: `README` (run, test, deploy in < 10 lines each), `CLAUDE.md` referencing this standard, `CHANGELOG`, ADRs in `docs/adr/` for decisions that constrain future work.

rules.section: 6F · Repo hygiene
rules.title: Protected main
rules.text: Protected `main`: PR required, gates green, no force-push; `CODEOWNERS` for platform core, tokens, migrations, CI and agent configuration (AGT-9).

rules.section: 6F · Repo hygiene
rules.title: Conventional commits
rules.text: Conventional commits. (The PR template itself is required by CLEAN-9 and HELP-7: standard rules touched, exceptions added, help/docs updated.)

rules.section: 6F · Repo hygiene
rules.title: Dependency licences checked
rules.text: Dependency licences checked (no AGPL/unknown in shipped code without a decision).

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Screen help
rules.text: **Screen help** for every routable screen/tab, in the registry, rendered by the shared help panel/sheet. Content lives in the registry (Markdown/JSON), not in widget code.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Field-level inline help
rules.text: **Field-level inline help** wherever a field, column, metric or setting isn't self-explanatory: helper text under the input, an `ⓘ` tooltip/popover for columns and metrics, units and allowed ranges stated, examples for formats. Keyed by field id in the same registry.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Errors teach the fix
rules.text: **Errors teach the fix.** Validation and error messages say what's wrong and how to fix it, map from CORE-7 error codes to registry text, show `request_id`, and link to the relevant help.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Empty states guide
rules.text: **Empty states guide** — say why it's empty and offer the next action (configure, import, create, run the job) — copy comes from the registry.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: First-run onboarding
rules.text: **First-run onboarding**: a short tour or checklist per major area; tour anchors reference stable widget/test ids and a test asserts every anchor resolves.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Living docs
rules.text: **Living docs** in `docs/user/<feature>.md` (one page per feature, docs-as-code, reviewed in the same PR as the feature); every registry entry links to its page; served in-app or on the docs site. Developer docs (`docs/adr/`, `docs/specs/`, `RUNBOOK.md`, API schema) are separate from user docs.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Help is tested and kept current
rules.text: **Help is tested and kept current:** (a) a test asserts every route resolves to a registry entry and every entry's doc link resolves; (b) a test or lint asserts every form field/column id used in screens has a field-help entry or is explicitly marked self-explanatory; (c) the PR template asks "help/docs updated?"; a UI change that alters labels, fields or steps without a help change is a review finding.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Help is searchable from anywhere
rules.text: Help is searchable from anywhere (command palette / help search), externalized for i18n with the rest of the strings, and accessible (keyboard, screen reader, both themes).

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Help usage is observable
rules.text: Help usage is observable: `help.open` / `help.search` events (LOG-1) with no PII; a search with no result is a docs backlog item.

rules.section: 6G · In-app help & documentation — every screen, every field
rules.title: Screenshots in docs are regenerated by the e2e suite
rules.text: Screenshots in docs are regenerated by the e2e suite (Playwright / integration tests), so they never show a previous version of the UI.

rules.section: 7 · Enforcement — make the standard mechanical
rules.subsection: 7.2 Banned-API rules (one per CORE row) — shipped in the kit
rules.title: New repos adopt the kit at creation
rules.text: New repos adopt the kit at creation; existing repos adopt with `--baseline` so only **new** violations fail, then burn the baseline down.

rules.section: 7 · Enforcement — make the standard mechanical
rules.subsection: 7.2 Banned-API rules (one per CORE row) — shipped in the kit
rules.title: A single line may be suppressed only with nosemgrep
rules.text: A single line may be suppressed only with `nosemgrep: <rule-id> -- <reason>`; anything broader goes in `docs/STANDARD_EXCEPTIONS.md` with an expiry. `.semgrepignore` lists only generated, vendored or third-party code.

rules.title: Declare the mode
rules.text: **Declare the mode** (§0A) in `standard.config.json` (`"mode": "quick" | "client"`; absent = client). Quick mode is allowed only while the app has **no** users outside the owner's team, is not in an app store or on a public URL (access-controlled previews are fine, WEB-17), and holds no personal data of third parties. The day any of these changes, the repo switches to client mode in the same PR and runs `APP_REVIEW.md` profile `standard` before release. The plugin's `SessionStart` hook warns when a quick-mode repo shows store or website deploy config.
